newsitem.title: USA: Asset-backed issuance seen thriving in '97 -- PSA.
newsitem.headline: Asset-backed issuance seen thriving in '97 -- PSA.

text.p: Issuance of asset-backed securities (ABS) is expected to reach record levels for the fifth consecutive year in 1997 following a projected surge of 30.7 percent in 1996, PSA The Bond Market Trade Association said in a report Tuesday.
ABS issuance should total about $141 billion in 1996, up from $107.9 billion reported in 1995, PSA said. And total issuance in 1997 is expected to reach $171.9 billion, it said.
The surge in ABS volume is due to stronger investor demand for short-term paper, the entrance of new issuers and innovative structures for securitizing a variety of assets, according to the report.
"Demand for ABS securities has been soaring as a result of the attractive yields, high credit quality and liquidity offered in this market," said Andy Nybo, director of market statistics at PSA.
Nybo, who authored the report, said yields on ABS issues are more attractive than those of corporate securities of comparable credit quality and maturities.
But he said the added yield comes with little additional credit risk because most structures have been credit-enhanced or over-collaterized.
Nybo noted that an increasing number of non-traditional issuers, such as municipalities and other types of esoteric assets from the private sector, should bolster ABS volume.
Additionally, securitization of student loans is expected to increase by about one-third in 1997, supporting total student loan-backed issuance projected at $13.1 billion, the report said.

Although the largest sector of the market, the credit card sector, has begun to diminish as the market has grown more diverse, issuance this year is projected to total $48.0 billion, up from 1995's $47.4 billion, PSA said.
Nybo projected auto loans and receivables to reach $33.7 billion in issuance by year-end 1996, a 19.6 percent market share.
"As more consumers opt to lease instead of purchase new cars next year, issuance is expected to grow another 15.5 percent to $33.7 billion," Nybo said in the report.
Nybo added that a lower luxury tax will likely provide an added boost to auto loan receivables for securitization.
The PSA report said that ABS issuance in home equity loans and revolving credit plan receivables doubled this year to an estimated $30 billion.
"Banks and finance companies have increasingly standardized their loan products, making securitization more efficient," it said.
A rise in home ownership and continued consolidation of consumer debt should lead home equity loans to a 32 percent increase next year to $39.5 billion, PSA said.
